title: TRANSPARENT- Transsectoral Patient Pathways in Acute and Emergency Medicine: Resource Optimization, Efficiency, and Measurability
summary:
Acute and emergency care is a crucial pillar of healthcare in Germany, representing a core competence of many cooperating players in providing basic care to the population. Emergency departments are the hubs between ambulance services, outpatient, and inpatient care. However, in Germany, it is currently impossible to track which patients enter the hub, why, when, and where, as well as which care structures they may have already utilized. Patients sometimes feel that they are shuffled from one place to another. But it is not only the patients who are burdened by this situation. The system itself is also under increasing pressure, with annual increases of around 4% in the number of ambulance call-outs and rising patient numbers in emergency departments, despite outpatient services being a part of everyday life. According to the AKTIN emergency admission register, the number of cases in 2022 ranged from 12,200 to 65,100 per participating emergency department, with an inpatient admission rate of 2.5%. The personnel- and resource-intensive care provided by rescue services, emergency rooms and emergency medical services requires measures to continue to meet the demand for timely medical assistance. 
A fundamental structural analysis of patient pathways in acute and emergency medicine is therefore required. With the establishment of a system analysis, excessive burdens and multiple uses can be defined and the effects of adjustment measures can be considered in order to make resource management more effective and adapt it to real conditions.  The TRANSPARENT project provides the basis for quantifying changes in the field of acute and emergency medicine. The project links routine data in order to quantitatively and cross-sectorally record patient pathways in acute and emergency situations in the model region of Aachen (city and urban region) and analyse them using process mining methods.  Qualitative interviews with relevant stakeholders supplement the identified patterns of utilisation. In addition, structured surveys of patients and medical staff are conducted to obtain information about perceived barriers to accessing acute and emergency care. The results can be used to evaluate the potential for identifying, directing and possibly relieving patient flows and to develop options for adjusting resource provision and specifically tailored education and information campaigns.

interventions.name: Routine data: Patients with acute symptoms in acute and emergency medicine in the Aachen region
Routine data: Patients with acute symptoms in acute and emergency medicine throughout Germany via the AKTIN emergency admission register

Surveys (active recruitment planned for this purpose only): Patients with acute symptoms in acute and emergency medicine in the Aachen region in emergency rooms and KV emergency services; employees in emergency rooms, KV emergency services and in the Aachen region rescue service.
